extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, engineers, instrument purchasers, students, and general scientifically-literate public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical criteria for designing, testing, purchasing, and using scientific instruments and for conducting/recording observational experiments (e.g., eclipse photography, tree-sap pressure measurements) as presented in a 1907 issue of Nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership admission (British Association for the Advancement of Science)
rubrics_metrics.description: No technical qualification is required on the part of applicants for admission as a Member or as an Associate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members pay an admission fee and an annual fee for attendance at meetings; Associates pay for each Annual Meeting they attend. Ladies are admitted on the same terms as others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for communications and advertisements to the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements and communications to the Editor and business letters for Nature should be addressed to the Publishers; Editorial communications to 'Physics', London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical submission/addressing instruction for correspondence with the journal (distinguishes business/advertising from editorial communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges and sizing rules for advertisements in Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified charges for advertisements (e.g., three lines in a column, per line, one sixteenth page, one eighth page, quarter column, half page, whole page) with first heavy-type line charged as two lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price schedule and rule about heavy-type first line; cheques and money orders payable to Macmillan & Co., Limited; Office address given. (Procedural constraints for submitting ads.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/performance features for laboratory electrometers
rubrics_metrics.description: Desired properties include deadbeat behaviour, small electrostatic capacity, high insulation, and quartz fibre suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad for the Dolezalek electrometer lists these features as selling/functional points; implies such properties are criteria when choosing an electrometer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extractor design and practical features (Layelle 'FLOW' extractors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extractor should keep the substance covered by solvent while a new flow of clean solvent is continuously moved directly through the substance, facilitating rapid and efficient extraction; cups of glass convenient for weighing; arrangement for distilling off solvent after extraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature's test: extraction found both rapid and efficient; practical conveniences (glass cups for weighing, built-in condenser/distillation arrangement) are highlighted as desirable features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anemometer recording performance (Lander's patent anemometer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives a record of wind velocity from a light air to a hurricane; every separate puff is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises range (light air to hurricane) and temporal resolution (each puff recorded) as performance criteria; sold complete with clock and certificate on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine recorder criteria (Jordan/Nepretti & Zambra patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorder should show both the duration and the intensity of sunshine on specially sensitized charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different patterns and prices offered; charts and illustrative reproductions available—duration and intensity are the measurement outputs the device must provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscope essential features for school/field/technical use
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical student/field microscope should be complete with rack-and-pinion coarse adjustment, micrometer fine adjustment, triple nose-piece, and substage condenser; available in cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature list and price cited for Voigtländer microscopes; implies these components are expected in a suitable microscope for advanced student/field work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality criteria for 'technical' school apparatus series
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparatus should be specially designed and made to stand hard work in school laboratories and produce accurate results, while costing little more than ordinary catalogue articles (which are described as of practically no service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisement contrasts robust, accurate 'technical' series with cheaper items that are poor service; suitability for practical student experiments is emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binocular field-glass design criterion (Busch 'Stabil' binocular)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed on principles that prevent it getting out of adjustment, thereby enabling binocular vision and reducing muscular eye strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability of adjustment and reduction of eye strain are presented as primary criteria for field-glasses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marine biological specimen supply standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The laboratory can supply animals either living or preserved 'by the best methods'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertised guarantee of supply and preservation quality; implies standards for collection, preservation, and conditioning of biological specimens for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eclipse/corona observational methodology (Philippeville expedition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of simultaneous photographs through two large Nicol prisms whose axes made 45° with the horizon and at right angles to each other to demonstrate radial polarisation; telescopic examination for detailed inner-corona structure; use of specially prepared screen to photograph 'coronium ring' and reveal jets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous orthogonal polariser photography provided unmistakable evidence of radial polarisation; photographic and telescopic methods combined to characterise coronal structures and composition hypotheses (e.g., 'coronium' or unknown element). These observational choices are presented as effective methods for studying the corona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tree-sap/transpiration experimental methods and measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments on suction and exudation at different levels and on the influence of the entry of air and water under pressure; direct measurements of pressure in intact vessels during active transpiration (e.g., in Wistaria) to test for continuous suspended water columns or high internal tensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings (no continuous suspended water columns or high internal tensions in tested trees during active transpiration) are based on these experimental approaches; implies direct intra-vessel pressure measurement and level-varied suction/exudation tests are appropriate methods to evaluate theories of sap ascent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic polarisation evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: To show radial polarisation of the corona, take two simultaneous photographs through polarizers set at right angles; compare negatives for differences in streamer visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: one streamer was traceable on one photo but not on the other, providing unmistakable evidence. This demonstrates a practical photographic approach to diagnosing polarisation patterns.
